title: Directed Clinical Practice II
description: This course is the second clinical experience in electroencephalographic (EEG) testing at an affiliated healthcare facility. The clinical experience provides students a supervised application of previously learned techniques and skills. The course builds on skills attained in the first clinical experience course including performance of EEG testing on clinical patients, medical record keeping and clinical history taking in a timely manner. The focus is on safe, legal and professional behavior. This course also fosters the development of communication skills and interpersonal relationships required for the healthcare field. Supervision of the students is provided by a neurodiagnostic technologist and/or physician of the affiliating institution and is coordinated by the college faculty. This course is designed for students enrolled in the Neurodiagnostic Technology Program.
outcomes: Students will be able to apply electrodes accurately within 30 minutes and get the patient's test performed in an acceptable time.
Student will be able to identify and monitor artifacts with 85% accuracy and identify normal EEG activity with 95% accuracy.
Accurately document all work, including calibrations, instrument settings, clinical findings, modifications to recording, and appropriate patient information.
objectives: Demonstrate professional behavior including willingness to adhere to policies, appropriate dress code and absence/tardiness reporting guidelines.
Conduct self in an appropriate ethical manner as a health care professional including maintaining patient confidentiality and safety at all times.
Seek instruction and use feedback to improve performance.
Demonstrate a positive attitude to the clinical experience.
Relate to patients in a positive manner to encourage patient cooperation and enhance attitude including good communication skills in explaining all procedures and expectations of the patient.
Maintain work area in an orderly manner including obtaining and replacing supplies as needed and keeping work areas neat and clean.

Calibrate the machine within 100% accuracy and be able to make all necessary adjustments to the instrument for accurate recordings, including the proper use of cal voltage related to sensitivities and calibrating all settings used during a test.
Apply electrodes accurately within 30 minutes, and get the patients test performed in an acceptable time as per the lab schedule.
Use appropriate machine settings to provide optimal recording as necessary.
Identify and monitor artifacts with 85% accuracy.
Identify normal EEG activity with 95% accuracy.
Recognize abnormal events such as slow waves, spike &/or sharp activity, and other common discharges.
Accurately document all work, including calibrations, instrument settings, clinical findings, modifications to recording, and appropriate patient information.
Write a description of each EEG performed with accuracy as determined when reviewed by a technologists.
content: Regard for safety of others and self (including proper body mechanics)
Arrival at clinic on time and completing scheduled day, including accurate timecard reporting
Notification to college and clinic of expected tardiness and/or absence
Use of feedback to improve performance
Positive patient communication including appropriate explanation of procedures and expectations of patient
Maintenance of work area in orderly manner
Application of electrodes in timely and accurate manner
Appropriate machine settings for optimal recording
Ability to write description of each EEG performed

Topics vary depending on the clinical assignment, but should include (if possible) EEG's on neonatal pediatric patients, adult patients, intensively ill patients and those with electrocerebral inactivity.
assignments: Professional journals including Journal of Clinical Neurophysiology and Neurodiagnostic Journal
Reports of patient's clinical history, test results, testing parameters and record keeping
Distinguishing between appropriate and inappropriate application principles of EEG.
Recognizing normal and basic abnormal EEG activity.
Reporting patient's pertinent clinical history, test results and testing parameters.
